{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=longitudinal+preference+evolution+path+dependence+autonomous+agents&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.65109/wvdn6068\", \"title\": [\"Preference-Based Multi-Objective Multi-Agent Path Finding\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) consists in computing a set of collision-free paths for a team of agents on a given graph while minimizing one objective, such as the sum of paths costs or the makespan. However, real-world applications may require the consideration of multiple objectives. Thus, in this work, we propose to address a novel extension of MAPF, Scalarized Multi-Objective MAPF (MOMAPF), that aims to optimize multiple given objectives while computing collision-free paths for all agents and incorporating the preferences of a decision maker over each objective. The preferences of a decision maker are reflected by a weight value associated to each objective and all weighted objectives are combined into one scalar to minimize. We introduce a solver for Scalarized MOMAPF based on Conflict-Based Search (CBS), Scalarized MO-CBS, that incorporates an adapted path planner based on an evolutionary algorithm, the Genetic Algorithm (GA). We also introduce three practical objectives to consider in path planning: efficiency, safety, and smoothness. We evaluate the performance of our proposed method in function of the input parameters of GA on experimental simulations.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.65109/wvdn6068\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2023, 5, 30]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.4337/9781848449268.00008\", \"title\": [\"Path Dependence versus Path-breaking Crises: An Alternative View\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.4337/9781848449268.00008\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2009, 7, 30]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1007/s10458-022-09593-3\", \"title\": [\"Preference-based multi-objective multi-agent path finding\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/s10458-022-09593-3\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2022, 12, 23]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.4337/9781848449268.00007\", \"title\": [\"Path Dependence: Some Introductory Remarks\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.4337/9781848449268.00007\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2009, 7, 30]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": fa…

{"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=empirical+mechanisms+distinguishing+path-dependent+preference+emergence+from+static+reinforcement+learning+policies&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"Learning-enabled collaborative intelligence in search and rescue robotics: a survey of paradigms, models, and challenges.\", \"abstract\": \"Search and Rescue (SAR) robotics increasingly depends on collaborative intelligence to operate effectively in dynamic, uncertain, and time-sensitive environments. Modern SAR missions require coordinated interaction among heterogeneous robotic agents as well as structured collaboration between humans and intelligent systems for perception, decision-making, and adaptive mission execution. This paper presents a structured narrative review supported by a systematic literature search of learning-enabled collaborative intelligence frameworks in SAR robotics, organized around three paradigms: human-to-machine (H2M), machine-to-machine (M2M), and machine-to-human (M2H) learning. The review examines recent developments in reinforcement learning, federated and decentralized learning, knowledge distillation, swarm intelligence, semantic communication, and the growing integration of large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) for knowledge grounding, transfer, and explainability. Beyond algorithmic advances, the analysis emphasizes deployment-oriented challenges including partial observability, communication constraints, uncertainty management, model reliability, and real-time operational requirements.
